about: The gospel of the Third Sunday of Advent. The delegation from Jerusalem asks three times, and John's answers grow shorter each time: I am not the Christ, I am not, no. Only after that does he say who he is, and he says it in Isaias' words. The Bethania of the last sentence lies beyond the Jordan and is not the one near Jerusalem where Martha and Mary lived.

s01.translation: At that time the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to John to ask him:

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s03.translation: He confessed and did not deny, but confessed: I am not the Christ.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s04.translation: They asked him: What then? Are you Elijah?

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s05.translation: He said: I am not. Are you the prophet? He answered: No.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s06.translation: They said therefore to him: Who are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say of yourself?

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s07.translation: He said: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: Make straight the way of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s08.translation: Those who had been sent were Pharisees.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s09.translation: They asked him: Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s10.translation: John answered them: I baptize in water; but among you stands One whom you do not know.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s11.translation: He is the One who is to come after me, who has precedence over me. I am not worthy to loosen the strap of His sandal.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s12.translation: These things were done in Bethania beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

w045.explanation: Latin has no article, so by itself it cannot say whether they ask about a prophet or about the Prophet promised to Moses. The Greek behind it has the definite article, and this edition reads it so — the gloss says the prophet.

w116.explanation: It means “one of you”, not “one of yours”.

w140.explanation: Following a biblical Hebraism, Latin points twice to the same Christ: “whose… His latchet”.
